rationales.F03: Gross caries is a common cause of both periapical granuloma and abscess, but more directly related to dental caries.
rationales.F04: A firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling is consistent with both periapical granuloma and abscess.
rationales.F05: No tenderness on percussion suggests a periapical granuloma over an abscess, which typically presents with more pronounced pain on percussion.
rationales.F06: A mild periapical radiolucency can be seen in both periapical granuloma and abscess, but is more characteristic of a granuloma.
rationales.F07: A provisional diagnosis of periapical abscess was made, directly implicating this condition.
rationales.F09: The description of the tissue as gelatinous, soft, and mushy is more consistent with a periapical granuloma than an abscess, which typically yields pus.
rationales.F10: A provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma was made, directly supporting this diagnosis.
